note: Wikimedia Commons, “St. Arseni of the Tver.jpg”; artist as recorded there: Unknown author — fetched 14 October 2026 at 1200px. The licence is as Commons records it. Identified as this saint because: Found by reading the Commons category off Wikidata — Q4069993, «Arsenius of Tver» — which gives `Category:Arsenius of Tver`. The file's title carries the see, «St. Arseni of the Tver», which is this folder's own stored Russian form «Арсений Тверской» and its cited line «Свт. Арсения, еп. Тверского (1409)», kept 2 March with the translation of his relics on 6 July. The same category holds the Menaion Reader plate «икона 07022 Арсений» — church-month 07 = March, day 2 — which corroborates the day independently; the named file is taken over it because it is 2988x3543 against the plate's 624, and because the plate's title is a bare «Арсений». NOT Arsenius of Serbia, Arsenius the Great or Arsenius of Elassona, none of which carries Tver. Commons describes it: St. Arseni of the Tver. Tempera and embroidery. Russia 19th century. 29x24 cm.
